focus: RAG retrieval/rerank latency risks and quota/orchestration scalability

findings.title: Rerank cache key omits model and manual rerank switches, causing cross-configuration stale hits
findings.suggested_fix: Include `modelCatalogId`, effective `secondaryEnabled` (budget + request override), and `secondaryTimeoutMs`/`secondaryMinCandidates` in the rerank cache key. Keep cache keys aligned with all inputs that can change rerank ordering/output.

findings.title: Retrieval executes full-index in-process scans per request (O(N) lanes + full sort), which will not scale with index size
findings.suggested_fix: Push candidate narrowing into persistence/search layer (lexical + vector + graph prefilter) and retrieve bounded top-K per lane. Replace full-array sort with top-K heap/select to avoid O(N log N) on every lane.

findings.title: Lane timeout guard does not cap CPU-heavy lexical/dense work because those lanes are synchronous
findings.suggested_fix: Make lexical/dense execution cooperatively cancellable (chunked async loop with deadline checks) or offload to worker threads/processes. `Promise.race` with `setTimeout` only limits async waits, not synchronous CPU loops.

findings.title: Replay persistence is synchronous in retrieval/rerank hot paths and adds multiple blocking upserts per request
findings.suggested_fix: Move replay writes to async/background queue (or batched fire-and-forget with bounded retry), and keep only essential latency-critical state on request path. If synchronous writes are required, batch replay records in one repository call/transaction.

findings.title: Replay store performs global in-memory scans for per-run lookups, creating O(total_replays) overhead on response mapping
findings.suggested_fix: Index memory by `runId` (e.g., `Map<runId, Map<replayKey, record>>`) instead of filtering the global map for each lookup. Also add bounded retention/eviction for in-memory replay cache.

findings.title: Query cache deep-clones values with JSON serialize/parse on every read/write, amplifying CPU and GC under load
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid JSON deep clone in hot path. Prefer immutable cached payloads, structuredClone with benchmarks, or shallow-copy targeted mutable fields only.

findings.title: Datasource orchestrator queue dispatch uses repeated linear scans and degrades at large queue depth
findings.suggested_fix: Use partitioned ready-queues (by workspace/datasource eligibility) or maintain a rotating cursor/priority structure to avoid O(n) scans per dispatch cycle.

residual_risks: `RagQualityService` and replay/query caches keep unbounded in-memory arrays/maps, so long-lived processes can accumulate memory and increase lookup costs over time.

Current retrieval architecture still computes lexical+dense+graph lanes in a single Node.js process; quota degradation reduces candidate counts but does not fundamentally cap worst-case CPU for large indexes.
testing_gaps: No stress benchmark asserting retrieval latency vs index cardinality growth (e.g., 10k/100k chunk tiers).
No regression test validating rerank cache-key isolation across `modelCatalogId` and `secondaryEnabled` toggles.
No load test proving replay write path can sustain target QPS without materially impacting p95 chat latency.
